methods.label: Distinguish the possible selection populations
methods.explanation:
If the student is selected uniformly from the 30 interest-group participants, the total number of participants is \(12+8+6+4=30\), and 12 are in the basketball group. The probability is \(12/30=2/5\).

The question does not specify that these participants are all the students in the class or that selection is restricted to participants. If selection is uniformly from the whole class of \(N\) students, where \(N\ge30\), the probability is \(12/N\). For example, a class of 40 students with 10 nonparticipants has the same group counts but gives \(12/40=3/10\).

Thus the recorded key \(2/5\) applies when selection is among the 30 participants. As written, the question does not determine a unique probability, and grading remains withheld because of this ambiguity.
